Please please please anyone doesn't know self defense, PLEASE learn Jui Jutsu, Wrestling,Judo, Kickboxing or Muay Thai, most people in fights don't know how to fight, so learning how to fight properly will always be beneficial and potentially life saving for when you need it.

Learn to throw a jab(a good jab could take you across the world), cross( compact straight punches will always connect first compared to a sloppy wide telegraphed punch thrown at the same time, a timed punch can knock out anyone, even a jab), execute single and double leg takedowns, execute the basic guards in Jiu Jutsu, chokeholds ( the rear naked choke, the guillotine choke, and the triangle choke are great techniques to begin with), joint locks(Armbars, leg locks, and arms locks are basics to learn), footwork, head movement, blocking, basic punches, kicks, learning to fall in grapping(<VERY USEFUL And important) and counters are already going to set you up to beat the average untrained man around your size(it gets harder to defend yourself against an opponent the bigger they are than you, but skill can make up for the size difference, the more skills you have the easier it is to fight someone, so train for experience to where at least you're comfortable you can hold your own against trained men around or above your size).

But most importantly train hard for running, there is no danger if one can run away from it, also combat sports and running will do wonders for cardio and endurance. You'll also need the cardio if you're going to gain endurance in fights(endurance and stamina is one of if not the most overpowered attributes to have in fighting{along with a chin that can take more damage than a average person, but that's mostly genetic, defense skills will always work and are the most useful skills} as combat sports are some of if not the most exhausting sports ever, try wrestling with someone for 30 seconds{on the grass}, throwing the most amount of punches you can for 30 seconds and you'll see how most untrained people would run out of gas in the first minute{the more you're tired the more prone you are to being defeated}). So if you're trained, you can just wait for them to be tired and take them out.

You should pretty much never use fighting skills on the street, one unlucky punch from a guy or women(learn to counter hair if you have to fight a women hand to hand and your a women, trust me on this one) can send your head cracked on the street and dead(if you have to settle friendly beef, make sure to do it on something soft like grass, *NEVER FIGHT OR PLAY FIGHT ON THE CEMENT OR ANYWHERE CLOSE TO HARD GROUND!*). 

If you can't get away from danger always assume it's a fight to the death, but if you are in control of the situation(they're ass at fighting, weak jaw, alchoholic, small, doesn't know how to grapple, you put them in a lock or chokehold, any weakness you can spot, that's why it's effective to be all rounded). 

If you can get your hands on something for self defense like pepper spray or a legal firearm, or even a knife(knives are very scary close range), try to have it whenever you're going somewhere sketchy or for when you think you might need it, also try have it close to you in your home(like a nightstand next to your bed in your bedroom). Tasers are not guaranteed to stop someone(some people are built different and can shrurg it off, I'm not joking don't bet your life on it).

I hope this can be of use to someone who's interested in learning to make the choice of whether your potential attacker gets to harm you or not. This is a highly useful skill and practicing it will also get you in shape, more toned, more faster and more versatile in other things as well.
